O Allah, adorn us with the adornment of faith, and make us guides who are guided."

I heard Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah sanctify his soul, say: "He asked for contentment after the decree, because then the reality of contentment becomes evident. As for contentment before it, it is only a resolve to be content if it befalls him, and contentment is only truly realized after it."

Al-Bayhaqi said: "We have also related in the supplication of the Prophet (ﷺ): 'O Allah, I ask You for health, chastity, trustworthiness, good character, and contentment with the divine decree (qadar).'"

The fifty-fifth: Contentment with the decree frees the servant from pleasing people through the displeasure of Allah, from blaming them for what Allah has not given them, and from praising them for what is in fact the pure bounty of Allah. Thus he would be wronging them in the first (by their contentment and their blame) and associating them with Allah in the second (by praising them). When he is content with the decree, he is freed from their blame and their praise, and contentment frees him from all of that.

'Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i related from 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Among the weaknesses of certainty is that you please people with the displeasure of Allah, that you praise them for the provision of Allah, and that you blame them for what Allah has not given you. Indeed, the provision of Allah is not drawn by the greed of the greedy, nor turned away by the aversion of the averse. Allah, in His wisdom, has placed comfort and joy in contentment and certainty, and placed distress and grief in doubt and displeasure." Al-Thawri related it from Mansur from Khaythamah from Ibn Mas'ud from the Prophet (ﷺ).

The fifty-sixth: Contentment empties the servant's heart and diminishes his worry and grief, so that he is free to worship his Lord with a heart light from the burdens of this world, its cares and its sorrows. Ibn Abi al-Dunya related from Bishr ibn Bashshar al-Mujashi'i, who was one of the scholars, that he said: "I said to a worshipper, 'Advise me.' He said: 'Cast yourself with the decree wherever it casts you. That is more likely to empty your heart and lessen your worry. Beware of being displeased with it, lest displeasure descend upon you while you are heedless and unaware of it, and it throws you in with those upon whom Allah is displeased.'"

Some of the early Muslims (al-salaf) said: "Leave off planning and choosing, and you will be in a pleasant life, for planning and choosing make life turbid for people."

Abu al-'Abbas ibn 'Ata' said: "Joy lies in Allah's arrangement for us, and all misery lies in our arrangement."

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: "Whoever is not set right by the decree of Allah will not be set right by his own decree."

Abu al-'Abbas al-Tusi said: "Whoever abandons planning lives in ease."

One of them said: "You will not find safety until you are in planning like the people of graves."

He also said: "Contentment is abandoning objection against the Lord in what He brings upon the servant."

'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "These supplications have left me with no concern for anything at all except in the places where Allah's decree falls." He often supplicated: "O Allah, make me content with Your decree, and bless me in Your measure, until I do not love hastening what You have delayed, nor delaying what You have hastened." He also said: "No desire of mine remains in anything except what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has decreed."

Shu'bah said: Yunus ibn 'Ubayd said: "I have never wished for anything at all."

Al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad said: "The content one does not wish for beyond his station."

Dhu al-Nun said: "Three are signs of submission: meeting the decree with contentment, patience at trial, and gratitude in ease. And three are signs of entrusting: suspending your will for His will, looking at what His arrangement brings about for you, and not objecting to the judgment. And three are signs of tawhid: seeing everything as from Allah, accepting everything from Him, and attributing everything to Him."

One of the knowers of Allah said: "The root of worship is three: do not reject any of His rulings, do not ask anyone other than Him for any need, and do not withhold anything from Him."

Ibn Shim'un was asked about contentment, and he said: "It is that you are content with Him as the one who manages and chooses, and content with Him as the one who apportions, gives and withholds, and that you are content with Him as God, Worshipped and Lord."

One of the knowers of Allah said: "Contentment is abandoning choice, the heart's joy in the bitter decree, and removing planning from the self until Allah judges for it or against it."

It was said: "The content person is one who does not regret what has passed of this world and does not grieve over it."

How excellent is the words of the poet:
The servant is one who frets; the Lord is one of decree;
Time turns in its changes, and provision is apportioned.
All good lies in what our Creator chooses,
And in choosing other than Him lie blame and ill-omen.

The fifty-seventh: If a person is not content with the decree, he falls into blaming the decrees, either with his body or with his heart and state. Blaming the decrees is blaming their Decreer, and so he falls into blaming people as well. Allah and people blame him, and he remains a blamer and a blamed. This contradicts servanthood ('ubudiyyah).

Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "I served the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for ten years. He never said to me about something I had done, 'Why did you do it?' Nor about something I had not done, 'Why did you not do it?' Nor did he say to me about something that happened, 'I wish it had not happened,' nor about something that did not happen, 'I wish it had happened.' When some of his household blamed me, he would say: 'Leave him, for what is decreed must happen.'"

His saying, "What is decreed must happen," covers two matters. The first: what the servant wished for and did not occur. The second: what occurred that he dislikes. It encompasses the loss of what is loved and the occurrence of what is hated. So if the first had been decreed, it would have happened; if the opposite of the second had been decreed, it would have happened. When the two states are equal in relation to the decree, the servant's servanthood is that the two states are equal for him in relation to his contentment. This is the requirement and demand of servanthood. It is clarified by the fifty-eighth: when the two matters are equal in relation to the contentment of the Lord, the Exalted, then this He has been pleased to have for His servant, so He decreed it; and that He has not been pleased to have for him, so He did not decree it. Perfect conformity is that the two are equal in relation to the servant, so that he is content with what his Lord has been content with for him in both states.

The fifty-ninth: Allah, the Exalted, forbade going ahead of Him and His Messenger in His religious legal ruling. That is the servanthood of this command. The servanthood of His cosmic, decreed command is that one should not go ahead of Him except where the prevailing benefit lies in that. Then going ahead is also by His cosmic and religious command. If He obligated patience or recommended it, or obligated contentment, and one left that, then he has gone ahead of His legislation and His decree.

The sixtieth: Love, sincerity and turning back to Allah (inabah) cannot stand except upon the leg of contentment. The lover is content with his beloved in every state.

'Imran ibn Husayn, may Allah be pleased with him, was afflicted with dropsy, and he remained lying on his back for a long time, unable to stand or sit. A hole was made in his bed for his needs. Mutarrif ibn 'Abd Allah al-Shikhkhir entered upon him and began to weep at what he saw of his condition. 'Imran said to him, "Why are you weeping?" He said, "Because I see you in this dreadful state." He said, "Do not weep. For the thing most beloved to me is what is most beloved to Him." And he said: "I will tell you something, perhaps Allah will benefit you by it, but keep it secret from me until I die: the angels visit me, and I am comforted by them, and they greet me, and I hear their greeting."

When Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, may Allah be pleased with him, came to Makkah, his sight having been lost, people rushed to him so that he would supplicate for them, and he began to supplicate for them. 'Abd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib said: "I came to him as a boy, and I introduced myself to him, and he recognized me. I said: 'O uncle, you supplicate for people and they are healed. If you supplicated for yourself, Allah would return your sight to you.' He smiled, then said: 'O my son, the decree of Allah is dearer to me than my sight.'"

Some of the knowers of Allah said: "A sin I committed, I have wept over for thirty years." It was asked, "What is it?" He said: "I said about something Allah decreed: 'I wish He had not decreed it,' or 'I wish it had not been.'"

Some of the early Muslims said: "If my flesh were cut with scissors, it would be dearer to me than saying about something Allah has decreed: 'I wish He had not decreed it.'"

It was said to 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Zayd: "Here is a man who has worshipped for fifty years." He went to him and said to him: "My beloved, tell me about yourself: Have you been content with Him?" He said: "No." He said: "Are you with Him?" He said: "No." He said: "Are you content with Him?" He said: "No." He said: "Then your increase is only in fasting and prayer?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Were it not that I am shy before you, I would tell you that your dealing for fifty years is corrupted."

He meant that He had not brought him near, so as to place him among those brought near, so that He would grant him the experiences of the knowers of Allah, such that his increase with Him would be the deeds of the heart, by which every beloved sought is attained. For contentment is the state of the successful, intimacy with Him is the station of the lover, and contentment is the attribute of the one who trusts. He meant that you, in his sight, are among the ranks of the companions of the right, so your increase with Him is the increase of the general deeds of the limbs.

His saying "his dealing is corrupted" may carry two meanings:
The first: it is deficient compared with the dealing of those brought near, which brought them these states.
The second: if it were sound and whole, without defect or deceit, it would have yielded for him intimacy, contentment, love and lofty states. For the Lord, the Exalted, is Most Appreciative: when a servant's deed reaches Him, He beautifies his outer and inner being with it, and rewards him with realities of knowledge and faith in proportion to his deed. So when he finds no trace in his heart of intimacy, contentment and love, he infers that it is corrupted and not free from afflictions.

The sixty-first: The deeds of the limbs are multiplied up to a known and counted limit. As for the deeds of the heart, their multiplication has no end. This is because the deeds of the limbs have a limit at which they end and stop, so their reward is according to their limit. But the deeds of the heart are continuous and uninterrupted, even if the servant's witnessing of them is hidden.

Ibn al-Qayyim's example: love and contentment are the state of the one who loves and is content, and they never leave him in origin, even if their effect is hidden. So the one who possesses them is in continuous increase. The increase of the content lover is connected to the lasting of this state for him. So he is in increase even if his limbs grow lax. Indeed, his increase in a state of rest and slackness may be greater than the increase of many people of voluntary worship, by an incomparable degree. This may bring its owner to the point where his increase while sleeping is greater than the increase of many people of night prayer, and his eating (is greater in increase) than the increase of many people of fasting and hunger.

If you deny this, then reflect on the increase of one who sleeps while mindful of God, and the standing (in prayer) of one heedless of God. God, glory be to Him, looks only at hearts, resolves and determinations, not at the outward forms of deeds. The worth of a servant is his aspiration and his will. Whoever is not pleased by anything other than God, even if he were given the whole world in its entirety, has a station; and whoever is pleased by the least portion of its portions has a (lesser) station, even if their deeds are identical in outward form. The deeds of one who inclines to portions (of this world) may be more numerous and more arduous. That is the bounty of God, which He gives to whom He wills. And God is the Possessor of great bounty.

The people of this matter have differed on a question: Is there a limit to which contentment (riḍā) reaches?

Abu Sulayman al-Darani said: "Three stations have no limit: asceticism (zuhd), scrupulousness (wara'), and contentment (riḍā)."

His son Sulayman disagreed with him—and he was a knower ('ārif), to the extent that some people preferred him over his father—and said: "Rather, whoever is scrupulous in everything has reached the limit of scrupulousness. Whoever renounces other than God has reached the limit of asceticism. And whoever is content with God in everything has reached the limit of contentment."

They have also differed on a related question: there are people of three stations:
One of them loves death out of longing for God and His meeting.
The second loves to remain (alive) for service and drawing near (to God).
The third says: "I do not choose. Rather I am content with what my Master chooses for me: if He wills to give me life, and if He wills to cause me to die."

They referred the matter to one of the knowers, who said: "The possessor of contentment is the best of them, for he is the least in excess and the nearest to safety."

There is no doubt that the station of contentment is above the station of longing and asceticism in this world.

What remains is to consider the other two stations: which of them is higher?

One group preferred the station of the one who loves death, because he is in the station of longing for the meeting of God and loving His meeting. And whoever loves the meeting of God, God loves his meeting.

Another group preferred the station of the one who wants to remain (alive) in order to carry out the commands of the Lord, exalted is He.

They argued that the first loves his portion from God, while this one loves what God wills from him. He is not satisfied with it, and has not had his fill of it.

They said: This was the state of Moses, peace and blessings of God be upon him, when he slapped the face of the Angel of Death, so that he gouged out his eye—not out of love for this world, but in order to carry out the commands of his Lord and His pleasure among people. It is as if he said: "You are His servant, and I am His servant. You are in His obedience, and I am in His obedience and in carrying out His commands."

Then we say, regarding the sixty-second aspect: the state of the content, submissive one encompasses both of these states together, with added submission and abandonment of choice. For he has become absorbed in his Lord's purpose for him—of giving life and causing death—beyond his own purpose in these two matters. Every lover is longing for the meeting of his beloved and preferring what pleases Him. He has taken hold of the reins of both stations and attained both states. And he says: "What I love most is what He loves most. I wish for nothing but His pleasure, and I choose nothing over Him except what He loves and is pleased with." This amount is sufficient for this place. And success is from God.

Let us return to explaining his words. He said:

The second: the cessation of contention with creation.

He means that contentment is only valid with the cessation of contention with the creatures. For contention contradicts the state of contentment and contradicts attributing all things to Him who holds the reins of decree and destiny. So in contention there are harms.

One of them: the quarrel that opposes contentment.

The second: a deficiency in monotheism, by attributing what one disputes over to a servant rather than to the Creator of all things.

The third: forgetting the cause and the reason that led to the contention. If the servant returned to the cause and the reason, his occupation with removing it would be more beneficial to him and more profitable for him than contending with the one through whose hands it befell him. For he—though he is an oppressor—is the one who empowered him over himself by his own wrongdoing. God, exalted, said: ﴿Why, when a calamity strikes you, though you had struck (the enemy) with twice as much, do you say, "From where is this?" Say, "It is from yourselves."﴾ [Āl 'Imrān: 165]. So He informed that the harm their enemy did to them, and their defeat, was only because of their wrongdoing. And God, exalted, said: ﴿And whatever calamity strikes you—it is for what your hands have earned; and He pardons much.﴾ [al-Shūrā: 30].

When the servant's insight gathers upon the witnessing of destiny, of monotheism, of wisdom and of justice, the door of contending with creation closes for him, except in what is a right of God and His Messenger. So the content one does not contend or reproach except regarding what concerns the right of God. This was the state of the Messenger of God ﷺ. For he never contended with or reproached anyone except regarding what concerned the right of God, just as he never became angry for his own sake. When the sanctities of God were violated, nothing could stand against his anger until he avenged God. So contention for the sake of the self extinguishes the light of contentment, removes its radiance, replaces its sweetness with bitterness, and muddies its purity.

He said: The third condition: freedom from asking creatures and from insistence.

That is because asking involves a kind of contention, dispute and opposition, and a turning away from the Master of harm and benefit to one who possesses no harm or benefit for himself except through his Lord. Within it is also a heedlessness of the Giver and the Withholder.

Insistence contradicts the state of contentment and its description. God, glory be to Him, has praised those who do not ask people insistently. He said, exalted: ﴿The ignorant one thinks them wealthy because of their modesty; you recognize them by their mark. They do not ask people importunately.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 273].

One group said: They ask people for what their need calls them to ask, but they do not press. So God negated from them the asking of insistence, not asking in general.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "If he has lunch, he does not ask for dinner; and if he has dinner, he does not ask for lunch."

Another group—among them al-Zajjaj, al-Farra' and others—said: Rather, the verse requires leaving asking altogether, because they were described as modest and recognized by their mark, without disclosing a request. For if they had disclosed a request, the ignorant one would not have thought them wealthy.

(Section)

Just as the servanthood ('ubudiyyah) divides into a special kind and a general kind, so too does qunut (devout obedience) divide into special and general, and so does prostration (sujud). Concerning the special qunut, the Exalted said: ﴿Is one who worships devoutly during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord?﴾ [al-Zumar: 9]

And concerning Maryam He said: ﴿And she was among the devout ones (al-qanitin)﴾ [al-Tahrim: 12], and this occurs often in the Qur'an.

And concerning general qunut He said: ﴿To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth; all are devoutly obedient to Him﴾ [al-Rum: 26], meaning: submissive and humbled.

And concerning special prostration He said: ﴿Indeed, those who are near your Lord do not disdain His worship; they glorify Him and to Him they prostrate﴾ [al-A'raf: 206].

And He said: ﴿When the verses of the Most Merciful are recited to them, they fall down prostrating and weeping﴾ [Maryam: 58].

And this occurs often in the Qur'an.

And concerning general prostration He said: ﴿And to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and their shadows at dawn and dusk﴾ [al-Ra'd: 15].

Therefore this unwilling prostration is other than the prostration mentioned in His saying: ﴿Have you not seen that to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, the creatures, and many of mankind?﴾ [al-Hajj: 18]

Here He singled out many of mankind for prostration, and in Surat al-Nahl He generalized it: ﴿And to Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of creatures, and the angels﴾ [al-Nahl: 49].

This is the prostration of humiliation, subjugation and submission. Every single being is subject to His lordship, humbled before His might, and subdued under His sovereignty, exalted is He.

(Section)

The Exalted said: ﴿Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know? Only the people of understanding (ulu al-albab) take heed﴾.

Indeed, no single creature has its high parts equal to its low parts; its heel is not equal to its eye, nor its head to its feet, and neither is fit for what the other is fit for. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the wicked and the good, the easy and the hard, the harmful and the beneficial. These are the parts of the earth: some of it is fit to be a polish for the eye, and some of it is fit for the kiln and the fire.

By this and the like, the perfection of power and the perfection of wisdom are known: the perfection of power is in creating opposites.

And the perfection of wisdom is in placing things in their proper stations and setting each in its proper place. The one who knows does not set power and wisdom against each other: if he believes in power, he impugns wisdom and nullifies it; if he believes in wisdom, he impugns power and diminishes it. Rather he links power with wisdom, and knows that both encompass all that Allah has created and will create. Just as nothing occurs except by His power and will, so nothing occurs except by His wisdom. And since human intellects have no way to comprehend this in detail, it suffices them to believe in what they know and witness of it, then infer the unseen from the seen and reason from what they know to what they do not know.

(Section)

Know that Allah, glorified is He, negated equality between the knower and other than him, just as He negated equality between the wicked and the good, between the blind and the seeing, between light and darkness, between shade and scorching heat, between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, between the mute, incapable one who has no power over anything and one who commands justice while he is on a straight path, between the believers and the disbelievers, between those who believe and do righteous deeds and the corrupters on the earth, and between the pious and the wicked.

These are ten places in the Qur'an in which He negated equality among these categories, and this indicates that the rank of the knower relative to the ignorant is like the rank of light relative to darkness, of shade relative to scorching heat, and of the good relative to the wicked.

And the rank of each of these categories is with its opposite.

This suffices for the honor of knowledge and its people. Indeed, if you reflect on all these categories, you will find that the negation of equality among them returns to knowledge and what it necessitates: in it preference occurs and equality is negated.

(Section: On convening an assembly containing a debate between a proponent of singing and a proponent of the Qur'an)

Each of the two parties presented his argument, and both agreed to submit to the judgment of one who preferred reason and religion over his own desires, and for whom the truth with which Allah sent His Messenger was dearer than anything else.

So he sat in the seat of judgment between the two adversaries, and looked with the eye of sincere counsel for himself regarding each of the two arguing parties. He set aside the zeal of the Jahiliyyah and the partisanship of the sect of the esoteric (Batiniyyah), and he took as allies those whom Allah, His Messenger and the believing servants take as allies: ﴿They were not its guardians; its guardians are none but the God-fearing, but most of them do not know﴾ [al-Anfal: 34].

This is the beginning of the debate.

The proponent of singing said: Allah has commanded His Messenger to give good tidings to those who listen to speech and follow the best of it. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So give good tidings to My servants, (17) those who listen to speech and follow the best of it. Those are the ones whom Allah has guided, and those are the people of understanding﴾ [al-Zumar: 17–18]. He said: The definite article "al-" in "al-qawl" (the speech) necessitates generality and comprehensiveness. The proof of this is that He praised them for following the good speech, and this encompasses every speech, so it includes the speech of listening (singing) and other than it.

The proponent of the Qur'an said: You ought to have revered and exalted the Speech of Allah, not applied it to the words of male and female singers and their companions among the wailers and wailing women, nor have it be understood as an incantation for adultery, a source of hypocrisy, a summoner to error and desire. For the corruption of this interpretation it suffices that no one among the Imams of Tafsir, across their different generations, has said it before you.

And there are many aspects which show its invalidity and show that it is impossible that by the speech of Him "from before it or behind it falsehood cannot come" there be meant these things:

The first: Allah, glorified and exalted is He, does not command, nor even permit, the listening to every speech, such that it could be said: the "lam" is for comprehensiveness and generality. Rather, among speech there is that whose listening is forbidden, and among it that which is disliked. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿When you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our signs, turn away from them until they engage in a different discourse. And if Satan causes you to forget, then do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people (68)﴾ [al-An'am: 68].

So He commanded turning away from listening to this speech, and forbade sitting with those who utter it.

And He said: ﴿And it has already been revealed to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being denied and mocked, do not sit with them until they engage in a different discourse; otherwise you would be like them﴾ [al-Nisa': 140].

So He made the listener to this talk like its speaker. How then could He, exalted is He, praise the listener to every speech?

And He said: ﴿Successful indeed are the believers, (1) who are humble in their prayer, (2) and who turn away from vain talk﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 1–3]. And He said describing His servants: ﴿And when they pass by vain talk, they pass by with dignity﴾ [al-Furqan: 72], meaning they honoured themselves by refraining from listening to it.

It is narrated that Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) heard the sound of amusement and turned away from it, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Ibn Mas'ud is noble."

So if Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has praised those who turn away from vain talk and pass by it with dignity, honouring themselves by not listening to it, how is it permissible to say that the "al-" is for comprehensiveness, and to attribute to Allah that He praised the listener to every speech? And He has said: ﴿And do not follow that of which you have no knowledge; indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart — about all of these one will be questioned (36)﴾ [al-Isra': 36].

He has informed that He will question the servant about his hearing, his sight and his heart, and He forbade him to follow (qafa) — that is, to pursue — what he has no knowledge of.

And if hearing, sight, speech and the heart are divided into what is commanded and what is forbidden, and the servant is accountable for all of that, how is it permissible to say: every speech in the world is such that the servant is praised for listening to it? The parallel of this would be to say: every visible thing in the world is such that the servant is praised for looking at it, given His saying: ﴿Say: Look at what is in the heavens and the earth﴾ [Yunus: 101], and His saying: ﴿Have they not looked into the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever things Allah has created?﴾ [al-A'raf: 185].

It is for this reason that Satan entered upon you and upon many of the ascetics through these two entrances: you were excessive in looking at the images that were forbidden to be looked at, and in listening to the words and sounds that you were forbidden to listen to. And Satan was not content with that from you until he adorned for you that you made what you were forbidden into worship, a means of drawing near and an act of obedience. This is the subtle trick of Iblis among you that was mentioned earlier, namely his saying: "I have among you the subtlety of listening and the companionship of youths."

The second aspect: the intended meaning of "speech" in this verse which you have cited as evidence is the Qur'an, as is shown by His saying: ﴿Do they not contemplate the speech?﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 68], and His saying: ﴿And We have certainly caused the speech to reach them﴾ [al-Qasas: 51].

So the speech which gives good tidings to its listeners and to those who follow its best is the speech which He caused to reach them and urged them to contemplate. The speech of Allah explains one part by another, and one part of it is to be understood in light of another.

The third aspect: the "al-" here is for definiteness of reference (ta'rif al-'ahd), namely the speech to which the addressee was called, was commanded to contemplate, and was informed that it would be conveyed to him, which is like the Book and the Qur'an.

The "al-" in it is the same as the "al-" in "the Book" (al-kitab). Likewise the "al-" in "the Messenger" in His saying: ﴿And the Messenger says: O my Lord, my people have taken this Qur'an as something abandoned (30)﴾ [al-Furqan: 30], and in His saying: ﴿Do not make the call of the Messenger among you like the call of some of you to others﴾ [al-Nur: 63], and His saying: ﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 92].

Is it then permissible to say that the "lam" in "the Book" and "the Messenger" is for comprehensiveness, so that it applies to every book and every messenger?

The fourth aspect: even if it is for generality in His saying: ﴿those who listen to the speech﴾ [al-Zumar: 18], it only generalises to the speech which Allah revealed and praised and commended, and commanded to follow, listen to, contemplate and understand. So it necessitates generality and comprehensiveness across all of this speech, for it necessitates the generality of what you have come to know and the intent of its referent.

The fifth aspect: the whole context from the beginning of the surah up to this verse is concerned only with the Qur'an. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise (1). Indeed, We have revealed to you the Book in truth, so worship Allah, making the religion sincerely His (2). Unquestionably, to Allah belongs the pure religion (3)﴾ [al-Zumar: 1–3]. So at the beginning of the surah He mentioned His Book, His religion, the good word and righteous deed. The best speech is His Book, and the best deed is sincerity of religion toward Him. Then He repeated mention of the two foundations in His saying: ﴿And those who avoid the Taghut, not worshipping it, and turn back to Allah — for them is good news﴾ [al-Zumar: 17].

This is sincerity of religion toward Him. Then He said: ﴿So give good tidings to My servants, (17) those who listen to the speech and follow the best of it﴾ [al-Zumar: 17–18].

This is His Book. So it encompasses the mention of His Book and His religion, just as the beginning of the surah does. So what have the speeches of male and female singers to do with this?

Then He said: ﴿So is one whose breast Allah has opened to Islam, and he is upon a light from his Lord? Woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah. Those are in clear error (22). Allah has sent down the best statement: a Book consistent, oft-repeated, at which shudder the skins of those who fear their Lord; then their skins and hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah﴾ [al-Zumar: 22–23].

So He praised the people of listening and ecstatic response to the speech and the discourse which He sent down, and He did not praise unrestricted speech and its listeners. Rather, the context includes praise of those who remember Him and listen to His discourse, just as He combined the two in His saying: ﴿Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should humble before the remembrance of Allah and what has descended of the truth?﴾ [al-Hadid: 16].

And in His saying: ﴿The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble, and when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith﴾ [al-Anfal: 2].

He, exalted is He, mentioned and explained in the Furqan the parables and proofs, so that we may remember by it, take admonition, contemplate it and understand it. He commanded us to listen to it and follow it, urged us to contemplate it, gave good tidings to those who listen to it and follow its best, and informed that He caused it to reach us so that we may be reminded by it, and informed that whoever does not contemplate it, his heart is one of the hearts upon which are locks. So what have the speeches of male and female singers to do with this matter?

Then Allah, glorified is He, repeated mention of the Qur'an in His saying: ﴿And the one who brings the truth and confirms it — those are the God-fearing﴾ [al-Zumar: 33]. Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih, from Mujahid, who said: "The one who brings the truth" is the Qur'an, and "confirms it" is the believer, who will come on the Day of Resurrection saying: "This is what You gave me; I acted upon what is in it."

So He mentioned the truthful one and the one who confirms it, praising both. Then He mentioned their opposites, namely the liar and the one who denies the truth, and these are two cursed kinds of speech, I mean lying and denying the truth. So how could one who listens to them be praised and deserving of commendation?

There is no doubt that the verbal and listening innovations which oppose what Allah sent His Messenger with of guidance and the religion of truth comprise two foundations: lying against Allah, and denying the truth. Indeed, championing whatever opposes that, whether it is listening or something else, comprises these two false foundations.

The sixth aspect: after that He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins; indeed He is the Forgiving, the Merciful (53). And turn back to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you, after which you will not be helped (54). And follow the best of what has been sent down to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive (55)﴾ [al-Zumar: 53–55]. So this "best" which He commanded to be followed here is the "best" which He gave good tidings to those who follow in the beginning of the surah, and it is the best of what was sent down in both places. A parallel to this is His saying to Musa in the Torah: ﴿So take it with strength and command your people to take the best of it﴾ [al-A'raf: 145].

All of this, when the sincere believer who counsels himself contemplates it, will know with certain knowledge that the Book, the speech and the discourse which Allah commanded to be listened to, contemplated, understood, and whose best is to be followed, is His glorious Speech, "from before it or behind it falsehood cannot come, a revelation from the All-Wise, Praiseworthy."

As for praising the listening to every speech, this is not fitting to be attributed to intelligent beings, let alone to the Lord of the earth and the heavens. The following clarifies it:

The seventh aspect: Allah, glorified is He, in His Book only praised those who listen to the Qur'an, commended this listening, and blamed those who turn away from it, and made them people of disbelief and ignorance, the deaf, dumb, who do not reason. He said: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent, that you may receive mercy﴾ [al-A'raf: 204]. He said: ﴿The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble, and when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith, and upon their Lord they rely (2)﴾ [al-Anfal: 2].

He said concerning those upon whom He bestowed favour: ﴿When the verses of the Most Merciful are recited to them, they fall down prostrate and weeping﴾ [Maryam: 58]. He said: ﴿And when they hear what has been sent down to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they have recognised﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 83]. And He said: ﴿Indeed those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down upon their faces prostrating﴾ [al-Isra': 107].

And He said in blaming those who turn away from this listening: ﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and dumb who do not reason (22). And if Allah had known any good in them, He would have made them hear; and if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while refusing (23)﴾ [al-Anfal: 22–23]. He said: ﴿And the example of those who disbelieve is like one who shouts to that which hears nothing but a call and cry — deaf, dumb, blind; so they do not reason (171)﴾ [al-Baqarah: 171]. And He said: ﴿And those who, when reminded of the verses of their Lord, do not fall down before them deaf and blind (73)﴾ [al-Furqan: 73].

This is abundant in the Qur'an, and the Book of Allah explains one part of it by another.

The eighth aspect: what is known in the Qur'an is the blaming of listening to speech which is singing, as He said: ﴿Do you then wonder at this discourse (59), and laugh and not weep (60), while you are sweeping (sāmidūn) [in pride]? (61)﴾ [al-Najm: 59–61]. Several of the Salaf said: it is singing; it is said "samada lana" meaning he sang for us.

So He blamed those who turn away from listening to the Qur'an and substitute for it listening to singing, as is the condition of the singing-worshippers who prefer the whistling (muka') and clapping (tasdiyah) to listening to the Qur'an, substituting for it listening to singing.

This is similar to those who wasted the prayer and followed the desires. And several of the Salaf said concerning His saying: ﴿And among people is one who buys idle talk (lahw al-hadith)﴾ [Luqman: 6]: it is singing.

The ninth aspect: you, the assembly of singing-proponents who argue with this verse, do not approve of listening to every versified and unversified speech; rather, you are among the greatest of people in disliking what you do not love of speech, both prose and poetry, and in recoiling from it. Your aversion from what you do not love and desire of speech is greater than the aversion of the one who disputes with you against listening to whistling and clapping. So why do you not include in the "speech" which Allah praised those who listen to and follow its best, those statements which oppose your desires and what you love? This, even though it is certainly better than the speech of singers and more beneficial to the heart in this world and the next. But the fault of this speech is that it opposes your desires and what you have innovated.

If the generality in the verse is intended, then your argument is refuted; and if it is not intended, it is also refuted. Thus the invalidity of your argument is made clear in both cases, and success is from Allah.

The tenth aspect: He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So give good tidings to My servants (17), those who listen to the speech and follow the best of it﴾ [al-Zumar: 17–18]. He praised them for listening to speech and following its best. It is known that much speech, indeed most of it, has no goodness in it, let alone being the best; rather, most speech throws its speaker face-down into the Fire.

The speeches which Allah has condemned in His Book are more than can be counted: impure words, false speech, speaking about Allah without knowledge, lying, slander, backbiting, mocking by nicknames, secret conferring in sin, transgression and disobedience to the Messenger, planning what He does not approve of in speech, a servant saying with his tongue what is not in his heart, saying what he does not do, idle talk, saying what Allah has not sent down any authority for, speech involving evil intercession, speech involving aid in sin and transgression, and similar speeches which are displeasing and hateful to the Lord, all of which are ugly with no good or better in them.

So claiming that the verse is general to include speech other than what Allah sent down to His Messenger, namely the Book and the Sunnah, is among the most blatant falsehoods.

The eleventh aspect: He, glorified is He, tied guidance to following the best of this speech, saying: ﴿So give good news to My servants, who listen to the word and follow the best of it. Those are the ones whom Allah has guided, and those are the people of understanding.﴾ [al-Zumar: 17-18]. It is known by necessity that guidance is only attained by one who follows the Qur'an, for he is the one whom Allah has guided. So where is the guidance in the statements of the male singers and the female singers?

In sum, the corruption of this view, which you have imposed upon the Book of Allah, attributed to it, and loaded upon it while it is innocent of it and it is not fitting for it to bear it, is known to everyone who has life and light in his heart. ﴿And whoever Allah does not give light, for him there is no light.﴾ [al-Nur: 40].

Then He repeated mention of the two foundations in His saying: ﴿And those who avoid the Taghut, not worshipping it, and turn back to Allah — for them is good news﴾ [al-Zumar: 17].

This is sincerity of religion toward Him. Then He said: ﴿So give good tidings to My servants, (17) those who listen to the speech and follow the best of it﴾ [al-Zumar: 17–18].

This is His Book. So it encompasses the mention of His Book and His religion, just as the beginning of the surah does. So what have the speeches of male and female singers to do with this?

Then He said: ﴿So is one whose breast Allah has opened to Islam, and he is upon a light from his Lord? Woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah. Those are in clear error (22). Allah has sent down the best statement: a Book consistent, oft-repeated, at which shudder the skins of those who fear their Lord; then their skins and hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah﴾ [al-Zumar: 22–23].

So He praised the people of listening and ecstatic response to the speech and the discourse which He sent down, and He did not praise unrestricted speech and its listeners. Rather, the context includes praise of those who remember Him and listen to His discourse, just as He combined the two in His saying: ﴿Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should humble before the remembrance of Allah and what has descended of the truth?﴾ [al-Hadid: 16].

And in His saying: ﴿The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble, and when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith﴾ [al-Anfal: 2].

He, exalted is He, mentioned and explained in the Furqan the parables and proofs, so that we may remember by it, take admonition, contemplate it and understand it. He commanded us to listen to it and follow it, urged us to contemplate it, gave good tidings to those who listen to it and follow its best, and informed that He caused it to reach us so that we may be reminded by it, and informed that whoever does not contemplate it, his heart is one of the hearts upon which are locks. So what have the speeches of male and female singers to do with this matter?

Then Allah, glorified is He, repeated mention of the Qur'an in His saying: ﴿And the one who brings the truth and confirms it — those are the God-fearing﴾ [al-Zumar: 33]. Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih, from Mujahid, who said: "The one who brings the truth" is the Qur'an, and "confirms it" is the believer, who will come on the Day of Resurrection saying: "This is what You gave me; I acted upon what is in it."

So He mentioned the truthful one and the one who confirms it, praising both. Then He mentioned their opposites, namely the liar and the one who denies the truth, and these are two cursed kinds of speech, I mean lying and denying the truth. So how could one who listens to them be praised and deserving of commendation?

There is no doubt that the verbal and listening innovations which oppose what Allah sent His Messenger with of guidance and the religion of truth comprise two foundations: lying against Allah, and denying the truth. Indeed, championing whatever opposes that, whether it is listening or something else, comprises these two false foundations.

The sixth aspect: after that He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins; indeed He is the Forgiving, the Merciful (53). And turn back to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you, after which you will not be helped (54). And follow the best of what has been sent down to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you do not perceive (55)﴾ [al-Zumar: 53–55]. So this "best" which He commanded to be followed here is the "best" which He gave good tidings to those who follow in the beginning of the surah, and it is the best of what was sent down in both places. A parallel to this is His saying to Musa in the Torah: ﴿So take it with strength and command your people to take the best of it﴾ [al-A'raf: 145].

All of this, when the sincere believer who counsels himself contemplates it, will know with certain knowledge that the Book, the speech and the discourse which Allah commanded to be listened to, contemplated, understood, and whose best is to be followed, is His glorious Speech, "from before it or behind it falsehood cannot come, a revelation from the All-Wise, Praiseworthy."

As for praising the listening to every speech, this is not fitting to be attributed to intelligent beings, let alone to the Lord of the earth and the heavens. The following clarifies it:

The seventh aspect: Allah, glorified is He, in His Book only praised those who listen to the Qur'an, commended this listening, and blamed those who turn away from it, and made them people of disbelief and ignorance, the deaf, dumb, who do not reason. He said: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent, that you may receive mercy﴾ [al-A'raf: 204]. He said: ﴿The believers are only those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble, and when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith, and upon their Lord they rely (2)﴾ [al-Anfal: 2].

He said concerning those upon whom He bestowed favour: ﴿When the verses of the Most Merciful are recited to them, they fall down prostrate and weeping﴾ [Maryam: 58]. He said: ﴿And when they hear what has been sent down to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they have recognised﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 83]. And He said: ﴿Indeed those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down upon their faces prostrating﴾ [al-Isra': 107].

And He said in blaming those who turn away from this listening: ﴿Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and dumb who do not reason (22). And if Allah had known any good in them, He would have made them hear; and if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while refusing (23)﴾ [al-Anfal: 22–23]. He said: ﴿And the example of those who disbelieve is like one who shouts to that which hears nothing but a call and cry — deaf, dumb, blind; so they do not reason (171)﴾ [al-Baqarah: 171]. And He said: ﴿And those who, when reminded of the verses of their Lord, do not fall down before them deaf and blind (73)﴾ [al-Furqan: 73].

This is abundant in the Qur'an, and the Book of Allah explains one part of it by another.

The eighth aspect: what is known in the Qur'an is the blaming of listening to speech which is singing, as He said: ﴿Do you then wonder at this discourse (59), and laugh and not weep (60), while you are sweeping (sāmidūn) [in pride]? (61)﴾ [al-Najm: 59–61]. Several of the Salaf said: it is singing; it is said "samada lana" meaning he sang for us.

So He blamed those who turn away from listening to the Qur'an and substitute for it listening to singing, as is the condition of the singing-worshippers who prefer the whistling (muka') and clapping (tasdiyah) to listening to the Qur'an, substituting for it listening to singing.

This is similar to those who wasted the prayer and followed the desires. And several of the Salaf said concerning His saying: ﴿And among people is one who buys idle talk (lahw al-hadith)﴾ [Luqman: 6]: it is singing.

The ninth aspect: you, the assembly of singing-proponents who argue with this verse, do not approve of listening to every versified and unversified speech; rather, you are among the greatest of people in disliking what you do not love of speech, both prose and poetry, and in recoiling from it. Your aversion from what you do not love and desire of speech is greater than the aversion of the one who disputes with you against listening to whistling and clapping. So why do you not include in the "speech" which Allah praised those who listen to and follow its best, those statements which oppose your desires and what you love? This, even though it is certainly better than the speech of singers and more beneficial to the heart in this world and the next. But the fault of this speech is that it opposes your desires and what you have innovated.

If the generality in the verse is intended, then your argument is refuted; and if it is not intended, it is also refuted. Thus the invalidity of your argument is made clear in both cases, and success is from Allah.

The tenth aspect: He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So give good tidings to My servants (17), those who listen to the speech and follow the best of it﴾ [al-Zumar: 17–18]. He praised them for listening to speech and following its best. It is known that much speech, indeed most of it, has no goodness in it, let alone being the best; rather, most speech throws its speaker face-down into the Fire.

The speeches which Allah has condemned in His Book are more than can be counted: impure words, false speech, speaking about Allah without knowledge, lying, slander, backbiting, mocking by nicknames, secret conferring in sin, transgression and disobedience to the Messenger, planning what He does not approve of in speech, a servant saying with his tongue what is not in his heart, saying what he does not do, idle talk, saying what Allah has not sent down any authority for, speech involving evil intercession, speech involving aid in sin and transgression, and similar speeches which are displeasing and hateful to the Lord, all of which are ugly with no good or better in them.

So claiming that the verse is general to include speech other than what Allah sent down to His Messenger, namely the Book and the Sunnah, is among the most blatant falsehoods.

The eleventh aspect: He, glorified is He, tied guidance to following the best of this speech, saying: ﴿So give good news to My servants, who listen to the word and follow the best of it. Those are the ones whom Allah has guided, and those are the people of understanding.﴾ [al-Zumar: 17-18]. It is known by necessity that guidance is only attained by one who follows the Qur'an, for he is the one whom Allah has guided. So where is the guidance in the statements of the male singers and the female singers?

In sum, the corruption of this view, which you have imposed upon the Book of Allah, attributed to it, and loaded upon it while it is innocent of it and it is not fitting for it to bear it, is known to everyone who has life and light in his heart. ﴿And whoever Allah does not give light, for him there is no light.﴾ [al-Nur: 40].

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 39, verse 22:

The people of guidance and faith have the expansion of the breast, its widening and its opening, while the people of misguidance have constriction of the breast and distress.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Is one whose breast Allah has opened to Islam, so that he is upon a light from his Lord...?﴾ [al-Zumar: 22]

So the people of faith are in light and in the expansion of hearts, while the people of misguidance are in darkness and in the constriction of hearts.

The point is that the life and illumination of the heart is the source of every good in it, and its death and darkness is the source of every evil in it.

(Section)

No servant is punished with a punishment greater than the hardness of the heart and distance from Allah. The Fire was created to melt hard hearts. The heart furthest from Allah is the hard heart.

When the heart hardens, the eye becomes dry. Hardness of the heart arises from four things:

Going beyond the measure of need in eating, sleeping, speaking and mixing with people. Just as when the body falls ill, food and drink do not benefit it, so too when the heart is sick with desires, admonitions do not benefit it.

Whoever wishes the purity of his heart should prefer Allah over his desire. Hearts attached to desires are veiled from Allah to the degree of their attachment to them.

Hearts are the vessels of Allah on His earth, so the most beloved of them to Him are the most tender, the firmest and the purest. Those who occupy their hearts with the world, if they occupied them with Allah and the Last Abode, they would roam through the meanings of His speech and His manifest signs, and would return to their owners with wondrous wisdoms and rare benefits.

When the heart is nourished with remembrance, watered with reflection and cleansed of impurity, it sees wonders and is inspired with wisdom. Not everyone who adorns himself with knowledge and wisdom and claims them is among their people; rather, the people of knowledge and wisdom are those who revived their hearts by killing desire.

As for one who has killed his heart and revived desire, knowledge and wisdom are mere borrowed words on his tongue.

The ruin of the heart comes from security and heedlessness, and its flourishing from fear and remembrance.

When hearts renounce the banquets of this world, they sit at the banquets of the Hereafter among the people of that call; and when they are content with the banquets of this world, those banquets escape them.

(Benefit)

The heart has six stations in which it roams, with no seventh: three low and three high.

The low ones are: the world that is adorned for it, the soul that prompts it, and the enemy that whispers to it. These are the stations of the low spirits, in which the hearts never cease to roam.

The three high ones are: knowledge that becomes clear to it, the intellect that guides it, and the God whom it worships.

And hearts roam through these stations.

[Chapter: on the causes of the expansion of the breast and its perfection for him ﷺ]

The greatest cause of the expansion of the breast is monotheism (tawhid), and in proportion to its perfection, strength and increase, the breast of its possessor expands.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Is one whose breast Allah has opened to Islam, so that he is upon a light from his Lord...?﴾ [al-Zumar: 22]

And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Whomever Allah wills to guide, He opens his breast to Islam; and whomever He wills to leave astray, He makes his breast tight and constricted, as if he were climbing into the sky.﴾ [al-An'am: 125]

So guidance and tawhid are among the greatest causes of the expansion of the breast, while polytheism and misguidance are among the greatest causes of its constriction and tightness. Among them is the light that Allah casts into the heart of the servant, which is the light of faith; it expands the breast, widens it and gladdens the heart. When this light is lost from the heart of the servant, it becomes constricted and distressed, and becomes in the narrowest and most difficult prison.

Al-Tirmidhi related in his Jami' from the Prophet ﷺ that he said:

"When the light enters the heart, it expands and opens." They said: "What is the sign of that, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Turning to the abode of eternity, withdrawing from the abode of delusion, and preparing for death before it comes."

A servant receives from the expansion of his breast according to his share of this light. Likewise the physical light and the physical darkness: the one expands the breast and the other constricts it.

Among them is knowledge, for it expands the breast and widens it until it is wider than the world, while ignorance brings constriction, confinement and imprisonment. The more the servant's knowledge widens, the more his breast opens and expands. This is not true of every knowledge, but of the knowledge inherited from the Messenger ﷺ, which is beneficial knowledge. Its people are the most open-breasted of people, the most expansive of hearts, the finest in character and the most pleasant in life.

Among them is turning in repentance to Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, loving Him with the whole heart, turning toward Him and delighting in His worship. Nothing expands the servant's breast more than this, to the point that he sometimes says: "If I am in Paradise in such a state, then indeed I am in a pleasant life."

Love has a wondrous effect on the expansion of the breast, the pleasure of the soul and the bliss of the heart, which none knows except one who has a sense of it. The stronger and more intense the love, the more spacious and open the breast. It constricts only when seeing the idle who are empty of this matter; their sight is a speck in his eye, and their company a fever of his spirit.

Among the greatest causes of the constriction of the breast is turning away from Allah the Exalted, the heart's attachment to other than Him, heedlessness of His remembrance, and love of other than Him. Whoever loves something other than Allah is tormented by it, and his heart is imprisoned in love of that other. There is no one on earth more wretched than him, more troubled in mind, more miserable in life, or more weary of heart. There are two loves: a love that is the Paradise of this world, the joy of the soul, the delight of the heart, the bliss of the spirit, its nourishment and its medicine, indeed its life and the coolness of its eye, and it is the love of Allah alone with the whole heart, with the attracting forces of inclination and will all directed toward Him; and a love that is the torment of the spirit, the grief of the soul, the imprisonment of the heart, the constriction of the breast, the cause of pain, misery and toil, and it is the love of other than Him, the Glorified.

Among the causes of the expansion of the breast is the continuance of His remembrance in every state and every place. Remembrance has a wondrous effect on the expansion of the breast and the bliss of the heart, and heedlessness has a wondrous effect on its constriction, confinement and torment.

Among them is doing good to creation and benefiting them with what one is able to give of wealth, status, personal effort and all kinds of kindness. The generous, benevolent person is the most open-breasted of people, the most pleasant of soul and the most blessed of heart, while the miser who has no kindness in him is the most constricted of people in breast, the most wretched in life, and the greatest in worry and grief. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck in the Sahih a parable of the miser and the one who gives charity: like two men wearing coats of iron. Whenever the one who gives charity intends to give, it expands over him and spreads until it drags his garments and covers his footprint; and whenever the miser intends to give charity, every link clings to its place and does not expand over him. This is the parable of the expansion of the breast of the believer who gives charity and the opening of his heart, and the parable of the constriction of the miser's breast and the confinement of his heart.

Among them is courage, for the courageous person has an expanded breast, a wide inner space and an open heart, while the coward is the most constricted of people in breast and the most confined of heart, with no joy or happiness for him, no delight and no bliss except of the kind shared with the beasts. As for the joy, delight, bliss and gladness of the spirit, these are forbidden to every coward, just as they are forbidden to every miser, and to everyone who turns away from Allah the Glorified, is heedless of His remembrance, ignorant of Him, of His names, His attributes and His religion, and whose heart is attached to other than Him.

This bliss and joy will become, in the grave, gardens and Paradise, while that constriction and confinement will turn in the grave into punishment and prison.

So the state of the servant in the grave is like the state of the heart in the breast: bliss and punishment, imprisonment and liberation. There is no consideration of one person's breast being expanded by a passing circumstance, or another's being constricted by one; for passing circumstances vanish when their causes vanish. What is relied upon is the quality established in the heart that causes its expansion or its confinement; that is the criterion. And Allah is the One sought for help.

Among them, indeed among the greatest of them: removing the impurity of the heart of blameworthy qualities that cause its constriction and torment, and that stand between it and attaining healing. For if a person adopts the causes that expand the breast but does not expel those blameworthy qualities from his heart, he will gain nothing of the expansion of his breast, and at best he will have two substances contending over his heart, and he will belong to whichever of them predominates over him.

Among them: abandoning the excesses of looking, speaking, listening, mixing, eating and sleeping, for these excesses turn into pains, griefs and worries in the heart, which confine it, imprison it and constrict it, and it suffers torment from them. Indeed most of the torment of this world and the Hereafter comes from them. So there is no god but Allah, how constricted is the breast of one who has shot an arrow at each of these afflictions, how wretched his life, how bad his state, and how intense the confinement of his heart! And there is no god but Allah, how pleasant is the life of one who has shot an arrow at each of those praiseworthy traits, whose aspiration revolves around them and hovers about them! For this there is a generous share of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed the righteous are in bliss﴾ [al-Infitar: 13], and for that there is a generous share of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And indeed the wicked are in the Blazing Fire﴾ [al-Infitar: 14].

Between these two are varying degrees which none can count except Allah, Blessed and Exalted.

The point is that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was the most perfect of creation in every quality by which the expansion of the breast, the widening of the heart, the coolness of the eye and the life of the spirit are attained. He is the most perfect of creation in this expansion, life and coolness of the eye, together with the physical expansion specially granted to him. And the most perfect of creation in following him is the most expanded, joyful and cool-eyed; and in proportion to his following him, the servant attains from the expansion of his breast, the coolness of his eye and the delight of his spirit what he attains. He ﷺ is at the summit of perfection in the expansion of the breast, the raising of the remembrance and the removal of burdens, and his followers have of that according to their share of following him. And Allah is the One sought for help.

Likewise, his followers have a share of Allah's protection of them, His preservation of them, His defense of them, His honouring of them and His support of them, in proportion to their share of following. Some are sufficient and some are abundant. Whoever finds good, let him praise Allah; and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame no one but himself.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 39, verse 29:

He means: if a slave among you has several owners who share him and who quarrel over him, and another slave has one owner, are these two the same? If you do not consider these two equal, how is it that you accept for yourselves many gods, making them partners with God, loving them as they love Him, fearing them as they fear Him, and hoping in them as they hope in Him?

(Section)

He, glory be to Him, argued against the ugliness of shirk (associating partners with God) by means of what the intellects recognize as the difference between the state of a slave owned by quarrelling masters who treat him badly, and the state of a slave owned by a single master to whom he is wholly devoted. Can intellects accept that the states of these two slaves are equal? Likewise, the state of the polytheist and the monotheist (muwahhid, one who affirms God's oneness, tawhid), whose servitude is wholly given to his true God, are not equal.

(Section)

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿God presents a parable: a man who has partners quarrelling over him, and a man belonging wholly to one man. Are the two equal in comparison? Praise be to God; but most of them do not know.﴾ [al-Zumar: 29]

This is a parable God has given for the polytheist and the monotheist. The polytheist is like a slave owned by a group of people who quarrel, disagree, and are mutually grasping. The "mutashakis" man is the one of narrow disposition. Since the polytheist worships many gods, he is likened to a slave owned by a group competing for his service, and he cannot possibly satisfy all of them. The monotheist, since he worships God alone, is like a slave belonging to one man, who is wholly devoted to him, knows his intentions, and knows the way to his pleasure. He is at ease from the bickering of co-owners over him; rather, he is entirely safe for his master without any dispute over him, together with his master's compassion towards him, mercy for him, care for him, kindness to him, and his management of his affairs. Are these two slaves equal?

This is among the most eloquent of parables, for one who is devoted to a single master deserves from him help, kindness, attention, and the management of his affairs in a way that the owner of quarrelling partners does not deserve. ﴿Praise be to God; but most of them do not know.﴾

(Fa'idah)

As for the death of the prophets and messengers, it was not because they were held in contempt by Him, but so that they might attain the place of His honour, find rest from the hardship and toil of this world and from the suffering inflicted by their enemies and followers, and so that the messengers might live on after them, each messenger seen after another.

So their dying is better for them and for the community.

As for them, it is for their ease from the world and their joining the Highest Companion in the most perfect pleasure and joy; especially since their Lord gave them the choice between remaining in this world and joining Him.

As for the nations, it is known that they did not obey them only during their lifetimes; rather they obeyed them after their deaths just as they had obeyed them in their lives, and that their followers did not worship them, but worshipped God through their commands and prohibitions, and God is the Living who does not die.

Thus, in their dying there is much wisdom and benefit for them and for the nations.

Moreover, they are human beings, and God did not create humans in this world with a form fit for permanence; rather He made them successors on the earth, one succeeding another. Had He left them to live on, the benefit and wisdom in making them successors would have been lost, and the earth would have become too narrow for them.

So death is a perfection for every believer, and were it not for death, life in this world would not have been good, nor would its people have known contentment in it.

Thus the wisdom in death is like the wisdom in life.

(Fa'idah)
