If you know the subtle and precise manner of its inference, it is this: sin inevitably leaves an effect, and this effect is removed sometimes by repentance, sometimes by erasing good deeds, sometimes by expiating afflictions, and sometimes by entering the Fire so as to be purified of its effect. Likewise, if its effect becomes strong and those things are not able to erase it, then entering the Fire is necessary, because Paradise does not contain a particle of impurity, and no one enters it except one who is pure in every respect. If some of the impurity of sins remains upon him, he is placed in the crucible of trial so that the gold of his faith is purified of its impurity, and then he becomes fit for the abode of kingship.

Once this is known, the removal of the requirement and effect of sin is sometimes achieved by sincere repentance, which is the strongest of means, and sometimes by taking the right (of others) from him and purifying him in the Fire. When he is purified by the Fire and the trace of filth and impurity is removed from him, he is given, in place of every evil deed, a good deed. When he is purified by sincere repentance, and the trace of the filth and impurity of sins is removed from him through it, he is more deserving of being given a good deed in place of every evil deed, because the removal of this filth and impurity by repentance is greater than its removal by the Fire, and more beloved to Allah. The removal by the Fire is a substitute for it, and repentance is the original. Therefore it is more deserving of replacement than what comes after entering (the Fire). This is clarified by:

The ninth aspect: The penitent has had every evil deed replaced by a good deed through his regret for it, since regret is itself repentance for that evil deed. Regret is repentance, and repentance from every sin is a good deed. So every sin he committed disappears through the repentance that takes its place, which is a good deed. Thus he has a good deed in place of every evil deed in this sense. Reflect upon this, for it is among the most subtle of aspects.

On this basis, this good deed may be equal in weight to that evil deed, may fall short of it, or may exceed it. This depends on the sincerity of this repentance, the truthfulness of the penitent in it, and what accompanies it of acts of the heart whose benefit and advantage exceed the harm of that evil deed. This is among the secrets and subtleties of the matters of repentance. This is clarified by:

The tenth aspect: The sin of one who knows Allah and His command may result in good deeds greater, more numerous, more beneficial, and more beloved to Allah than his being kept from that sin, through humility, brokenness, fear, turning back in repentance, regret, making amends, and confronting the enemy with a good deed or good deeds greater than it, until Satan says: "Would that I had not led him into what I led him into." Satan regrets leading him into sin, just as the one who committed it regrets committing it. But how far apart are the two regrets! Allah, the Exalted, loves from His servant that he enrage His enemy and cause him grief, as has already been mentioned, that this is among the aspects of servanthood and among the secrets of repentance. So the servant enrages the enemy through repentance and making amends, and what Allah loves comes about through repentance and the increase of deeds that follow it. This results in a good deed being placed in the sin's place, indeed good deeds.

Reflect on His saying: "Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds," and He did not say "in place of each one, one." This permits that a single evil deed be replaced with several good deeds according to the state of the one who makes the replacement.

As for the hadith, the one who was punished for his sins did not replace them in this world with good deeds through sincere repentance and its consequences. So he had nothing that could make good deeds in place of his evil deeds, and he was given one good deed in place of each evil deed. The Prophet ﷺ was silent about his major sins, and when he reached them he laughed, and did not explain what Allah does with them. He informed us that Allah replaces each minor sin with a good deed. However, there is a subtle indication in the hadith that this replacement encompasses both his major and minor sins, from two aspects:

**1.** One of them is His saying: ﴿Turn away from Him the major sins﴾. This indicates that when he sees the minor sins being replaced, he remembers them and hopes for their replacement. So the replacement of his major sins has a greater effect on him than the replacement of minor sins, and he rejoices and is pleased with it even more.

**2.** The second is the Prophet's (ﷺ) laughter when this was mentioned. This laughter indicates amazement at the kindness that is shown to him, and at what he admits of his own sins, without being pressed about them or questioned about them, since only the minor sins were presented to him.

So blessed is Allah, the Lord of the worlds, the most generous of the generous, the most noble of the noble, the Righteous, the Gentle, who is affectionate toward His servants with all kinds of kindness, and who conveys it to them from every direction and in every manner. There is no god but Him, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

**(Section)**

Many people explain *tawbah* (repentance) only as resolving not to return to the sin, abandoning it immediately, and regretting it in the past. If the matter involves the rights of a human being, then a fourth thing is necessary: seeking to be absolved of it (*al-tahallul*).

What they have mentioned is part of the meaning of *tawbah*, indeed a condition of it. Otherwise, *tawbah* in the speech of Allah and His Messenger, as it includes that, also includes the determination to do what is commanded and to commit to it. A person is not a penitent merely by abandoning the sin, resolving, and regretting it, until there is in him the firm resolve to do what is commanded and to carry it out. This is the reality of *tawbah*, and it is a name for the combination of both matters. However, when it is paired with doing what is commanded, it is an expression of what they mentioned. When it stands alone, it includes both matters. It is like the word *taqwa* (God-consciousness), which, when used alone, requires doing what Allah has commanded and abstaining from what Allah has forbidden, and when it is paired with doing what is commanded, it requires refraining from what is prohibited.

The reality of *tawbah* is returning to Allah by committing to doing what He loves and abandoning what He dislikes. It is a return from what is hated to what is loved. So returning to what is loved is part of its meaning, and returning away from what is hated is the other part. For this reason, Allah, glorified is He, tied absolute success to doing what is commanded and abandoning what is forbidden through it, saying: ﴿And turn to Allah in repentance all together, O believers, that you may succeed﴾ [al-Nur: 31].

So every penitent is successful, and no one is successful except one who does what he is commanded and abandons what he is forbidden. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever does not repent, it is those who are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Hujurat: 11].

The one who abandons what is commanded is a wrongdoer, just as the one who commits what is forbidden is a wrongdoer. The removal of the name of wrongdoing from him occurs only through *tawbah* that encompasses both matters. So people are of two kinds: a penitent, or a wrongdoer, and nothing else. The penitents are ﴿those who worship, who praise, who travel, who bow, who prostrate, who enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil, and who observe the limits of Allah﴾ [al-Tawbah: 112].

So observing the limits of Allah is part of *tawbah*, and *tawbah* is the totality of these matters. He was named a penitent only because he returned from Allah's prohibition to His command, and from His disobedience to His obedience, as has been mentioned.

Therefore, *tawbah* is the reality of the religion of Islam, and the whole religion enters into the meaning of *tawbah*. By this, the penitent deserves to be the beloved of Allah, for Allah loves those who repent and loves those who purify themselves. Allah loves only the one who does what He has commanded and abandons what He has forbidden.

Therefore, *tawbah* is the return from what Allah dislikes, outwardly and inwardly, to what He loves, outwardly and inwardly. Its meaning includes Islam, *iman* (faith), and *ihsan* (excellence in worship), and it encompasses all the spiritual stations (*maqamat*). For this reason it is the goal of every believer, the beginning and the end of the matter, as has been mentioned. It is the goal for which creation was brought into being. Commanding and tawhid (affirmation of Allah's oneness) are part of it; indeed, they are its greatest part, upon which its structure rests.

Most people do not know the value of *tawbah* or its reality, let alone practising it in knowledge, action, and state. Allah, exalted is He, has not bestowed His love upon those who repent except that they are the elite of creation in His sight.

Were it not that *tawbah* is a comprehensive name for the laws of Islam and the realities of faith, the Lord, exalted is He, would not rejoice at the repentance of His servant with such great joy. Thus, everything that people speak of regarding the spiritual stations and states is a detailed explanation of *tawbah* and its effects.

**(Section)**

Said in (*Hidayat al-Hayara*):

The questioner said:

"We see in your religion that the greatest abominations are found among those who are most knowledgeable and most learned in your religion, such as adultery, sodomy, betrayal, envy, stinginess, treachery, cowardice, arrogance and vanity, scarcity of scrupulousness and certainty, scarcity of mercy, manliness and honour, excessive anxiety, greed for this world, and laziness in good deeds. This state contradicts the tongue of speech."

The answer comes from several aspects:

**First:** It may be said: what burden is there upon the noble Messengers for the sins of their nations and followers? Does that detract anything from their prophethood, or require a change in the nature of their message? Has anyone been spared from sins of all their kinds and types except the Messengers and Prophets, peace be upon them? Is it permissible to reject their message and deny them because of the disobedience of some of their followers? Is this not among the most ugly forms of obstinacy? It is like a sick man whose sincere physician invited him to a means by which he could attain the utmost health, and he said: "If I were a physician, these people would not be sick!" Are the Messengers obliged to heal all the sick, so that no sick person remains in the world? Has anyone been obstinate toward the Messengers with such obstinacy?

**The second aspect:** Sins or disobedience are something shared among nations. They have always existed in the world among all classes of the children of Adam: the knowledgeable and the ignorant, the ascetic and the worldly, the ruler and the ruled. This is not a matter peculiar to this nation, so that this nation and its Prophet should be discredited by it.

**The third aspect:** Sins and disobedience do not contradict faith in the Messengers. Rather, Islam and faith, along with sins and disobedience, may coexist in the servant, so this and that are both present in him. Disobedience does not contradict faith in the Messengers, although it detracts from its perfection and completeness.

**The fourth aspect:** Sins are forgiven through sincere repentance. Even if a servant's sins reached the clouds of the sky and the number of the sand and pebbles, then repented from them, Allah would accept his repentance. Allah, exalted is He, said: {Say, O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins}.

This applies to the penitent, and that repentance erases what came before it, and the penitent from sin is like one who has no sin. Tawhid also expiates sins, as in the authentic hadith: "Son of Adam, if you meet Me with sins as large as the earth, and then meet Me without associating anything with Me, I will meet you with forgiveness as great as it." So the sins of Muslims are the sins of one who affirms Allah's oneness. If tawhid is strong enough to erase their effects completely, well; otherwise, the tawhid they possess will bring them out of the Fire if they are punished for their sins.

As for the polytheists and disbelievers, their shirk and disbelief nullify their good deeds, so they do not meet their Lord with a good deed through which they hope for salvation, and nothing from the forgiveness of their sins follows for them. Allah, blessed and exalted is He, said: {Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills}. And Allah, exalted is He, said concerning the disbelievers and polytheists: {And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make it scattered dust}. And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah refuses to accept a deed from a polytheist."

So the effects of sins are removed through sincere repentance, pure tawhid, erasing good deeds, afflictions that expiate them, and the intercession of intercessors for the monotheists. The final outcome, if one is punished for what remains upon him of them, is that his tawhid brings him out of the Fire. As for associating partners with Allah and disbelief in the Messenger, it nullifies all good deeds, such that no good deed remains with it.

**The fifth aspect:** It may be said to the one who raises this question, if he is from the wrathful nation, brothers of the monkeys: Is he not ashamed to raise this question, when his fathers and ancestors witnessed every day signs that no other nation had seen? Allah split the sea for them and saved them from their enemy, and before their feet were dry from the sea water, they said to Moses: "Make for us a god just as they have gods." He said: "Indeed, you are a people who are ignorant."

When he went to the appointed time with his Lord, they did not wait; after he left, they worshipped the calf made of gold. His brother Aaron was overpowered by them and could not object to them. Even though they witnessed wonders, and revelation was among them, they intended many times to stone Moses and his brother Aaron. When he called them to jihad, they said: {So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are sitting here}.

They harmed Moses in every kind of harm, until they said: "He is a man with a swollen scrotum (*adar*)." This was because he used to bathe alone. One day he bathed and placed his garment on a rock, and the rock fled with his garment, and he ran after it naked, until the Children of Israel saw his private parts, and they saw him as the most beautiful of Allah's creation when he was unclothed.

When his brother Aaron died, they said: "Moses killed him and hid him." So the angels lifted his coffin between the sky and the earth until they saw him dead. They preferred to return to Egypt and to slavery, so that they could be satisfied with eating meat, onions, cucumbers, and lentils. This is what they say among themselves.

What Allah related about them is that they preferred that over the manna and quails, and that they indulged in adultery while Moses was among them and their enemy was facing them, until they grew weak against them and did not prevail over them. Their worship of idols after the era of Joshua son of Nun is well known. Their trickery in catching fish on the Sabbath, do not forget it, until they were transformed into despised monkeys. Their killing of the prophets without right, such that they killed seventy prophets in one day at the beginning of the day, and then set up the market at its end, as if they had slaughtered sheep, is a well-known matter.

Their killing of Yahya son of Zakariya, and their sawing him with a saw.

Their persistence in great sins, their agreement to change many of the laws of the Torah, and their accusation of Lot that he had intercourse with his two daughters and fathered children by them.

Their accusation of Joseph that he undid his trousers and sat with the wife of the Aziz in the position of a woman with a man, until the wall split and the hand of Jacob appeared to him while he was biting on his fingertips. So he stood up and fled. Had the most debauched and wicked of people seen this, he would have stood up and not fulfilled his desire.

Their obedience to the one who rebelled against the son of Solomon son of David, when he set up for them two golden calves, and all of them bowed down to worship them, until war broke out between them and the believers who were with the son of Solomon. In a single battle, thousands upon thousands of them were killed.

Are the worshippers of rams and cows not ashamed to reproach the monotheists for their sins? Are the descendants of the murderers of the prophets not ashamed to reproach the fighters against the enemies of Allah? Where are the descendants of those whose fathers' swords dripped with the blood of prophets, from those whose swords drip with the blood of disbelieving polytheists? Is not the one who says in his prayer to his Lord, "Wake up, how long you sleep! Rise from your slumber," thereby disparaging and offending Him, ashamed to reproach the one who says in his prayer: "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, Master of the Day of Judgment. You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help"?

Even if the sins of Muslims reached the number of pebbles, sand, dust, and breaths, they would not reach the level of killing a single prophet, nor would they reach the statement of the brothers of the monkeys that "Allah is poor and we are rich," their saying "Ezra is the son of Allah," their saying "We are the sons of Allah and His beloved," their saying that Allah wept over the Flood until His eyes became inflamed from weeping and the angels began to visit Him, their saying that He bit His fingertips over that, and their saying that He regretted creating mankind and was distressed when He saw their disobedience and wrongdoing.

And greater than all of that is the attribution of all this to the Torah which He sent down to His interlocutor (Kalim, Moses). Even if the sins of the Muslims reached what they reached, they would be, in comparison to that, like a spit in the sea. And do not forget the story of their forefathers with Shaʼul (Saul), who rebelled against Dawud (David): the great majority of them joined him and fought alongside him against Dawud. Then, when they returned to the obedience of Dawud, and their delegations and armies came seeking forgiveness and apologizing, to the point that they competed to be first to reach him, one of them went forth and called out at the top of his voice: "We have no share in Dawud, nor any portion in Shaʼul. Let each of you go back to his tent, O Israelites!" And it was not long before the entire army of the Children of Israel went off to their tents because of his words. When this crier was killed, all the armies returned to the service of Dawud. The people were nothing but like a rabble of base men, whom a drum gathers and a stick disperses.

(Excellent point of benefit)

The Mu'tazilites argued for the createdness of the Qur'an from His saying, ﴿Allah is the Creator of all things﴾, and similar verses.

Most scholars answered that this is a general statement (ʿāmm) that is specified (makhṣūṣ), and that it excludes the point under dispute, just as it excludes other attributes such as knowledge and the like.

Ibn ʿAqīl said in al-Irshād: "It occurred to me that the Qur'an is not encompassed by this statement, and it is not fit to be encompassed by it,"

and he said: "Because by it was established the firm conveying of the information that He is the Creator of all things, and what is established by a firm conveying and informing is not included under the information itself."

He said: "If a person said, 'I will not speak today except that it is a lie,' his statement about that would not be included under what he informed of."

I say: Then I reflected on this and found it mentioned in the words of the Exalted concerning the story of Maryam:

﴿So if you see any human, say, "Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast, so I will not speak today to any human being."﴾

She was only commanded to say that so that she would not be asked about her child. Her saying ﴿I will not speak today to any human being﴾ conveys the information that she does not speak to humans, yet what she informed of is not included under the information; otherwise her statement would contradict her vow.

(Section)

The verified position is that the attributes of the Lord, exalted is His majesty, are included in the meaning of His name. So His name Allah, and the Lord, and the God, are not names for a bare essence having no attribute whatsoever. This bare essence cannot exist; the mind only supposes it as it supposes impossible things, and then passes judgment upon it. The name "Allah," glorified is He, and "the Lord" and "the God," are names for an essence that possesses all attributes of perfection and all descriptions of majesty, such as knowledge, power, life, will, speech, hearing, sight, subsistence, eternity, and all perfection that Allah deserves by His essence. Thus His attributes are included in the meaning of His name. Stripping the attributes from the essence, or the essence from the attributes, is a supposition and a mental fiction with no reality. It is a mere notional matter with no benefit, and no knowledge, faith, or understanding follows from it, nor is it knowledge in itself. With this the Salaf answered the Jahmiyya when they argued for the createdness of the Qur'an by His saying, ﴿Allah is the Creator of all things﴾.

They said: "The Qur'an is a thing."

The Salaf answered them that the Qur'an is His speech, His speech is among His attributes, and His attributes are included in the meaning of His name, like His knowledge, power, life, hearing, sight, face, and hands. So Allah is not a name for an essence without description, attribute, act, face, or hands. That is a non-existent god, supposed in minds, with no existence in reality, like the god of the Jahmiyya, whom they supposed to be neither outside the world nor inside it, neither joined to it nor separate from it, neither immanent in it nor transcendent over it. And like the god of the philosophers, whom they supposed to be an absolute existence not particularized by any attribute or description, having no will, power, volition, or speech. And like the god of the Unificationists (al-Ittihādiyya), whom they supposed to be an existence pervading existents, manifest in them, being the very essence of their existence. And like the god of the Christians, whom they supposed had taken a consort and a son, and clothed himself in the humanity of his son, and made it a veil.

All these gods are fabrications of their minds. The God of the worlds in truth is He to whom the Messengers called, and whom they made known by His names, attributes, and acts, above His heavens upon His Throne, distinct from His creation, described with every perfection, exalted above every deficiency, having no likeness, no partner, no helper, and no one intercedes with Him except by His permission: ﴿He is the First and the Last, the Outward and the Inward, and He is Knower of all things﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 3].

Self-sufficient in His essence beyond all that is other than Him, and all that is other than Him is needy of Him in its essence.

(Section)

The fourth level of the levels of qadar (divine decree) is Allah's creation of the acts of accountable persons, and their falling under His power and will just as they fall under His knowledge and His Book. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is Guardian over all things.﴾

This is a general statement that is preserved, and nothing of the world is excluded from it, whether its entities, its acts, its movements, or its stillnesses. It is not specified as applying only to His essence and attributes, for He is the Creator by His essence and attributes, and all else is created by Him.

The wording distinguishes between the Creator and the created. His attributes, glorified is He, are included in the meaning of His name, for (Allah) is the name of the God described by every attribute of perfection, exalted above every attribute of deficiency and likeness.

The world consists of two kinds: entities and acts. He is the Creator of its entities and of what proceeds from them of acts, just as He is the Knower of the details of that. Nothing of it falls outside His knowledge, His power, or His creation and will.

The Qadariyya said: "We say that Allah is the Creator of the acts of the servants, not in the sense that He originates and brings them into being, but in the sense that He decrees them, for khalq means taqdīr (measuring out), as He said: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators (khāliqīn)﴾."

And a poet said:

"You do indeed measure out what you create, *** and some people create but do not measure out (fara)."

That is, you indeed carry out what you have decreed and execute it by your resolve and power, while some people decree but have neither strength nor resolve to execute and carry out what they have decreed. So Allah the Exalted decrees the acts of the servants, and they are the ones who brought them into existence and originated them.

The People of the Sunna said: Your early authorities deny Allah's decree of the servants' acts altogether, so they cannot answer with that. Whoever among you acknowledges decree, it is a decree that does not return to effective causation; it is merely knowledge of them and reporting about them. For decree, in your view, is not making them according to such and such a measure, since this, in your view, is not something decreed for the Lord nor made by Him; rather it is the servant's own making and origination. So decree reduces to mere knowledge and report.

This is not called creation (khalq) in the language of any nation. If it were creation, then whoever knew a thing, knew its names and attributes, and reported about it, would be its creator. The decree you affirm, if it includes effective influence in bringing the act into being, then it contradicts your doctrine; and if it includes no effective influence in its bringing into being, then it reduces to pure knowledge and report.

The Qadariyya said: His saying ﴿Allah is the Creator of all things﴾ is a general statement by which a specific sense is intended, especially since you yourselves said that the Qur'an is not included in this generality, though it is among the greatest and most august of things. So we specify the acts of the servants by the proofs indicating that they are their acts and their doing.

The People of the Sunna said: The Qur'an is the speech of Allah, the Glorified, and His speech is one of His attributes and the attributes of the Creator; and His essence and attributes are not included in the created. For the Creator is other than the created. So there is no specification here at all. Rather Allah, by His essence and attributes, is the Creator, and all besides Him is created. That is a generality with no specification in any respect, since there is only the Creator and the created, and Allah alone is the Creator, and all else besides Him is created. As for the proofs indicating that the acts of the servants are their handiwork, and that their acts are those subsisting in them, and that they are the ones who did them, all of these are true, and we act according to their implications. But it does not follow that they are acts of theirs and also created and made by Allah. For the act is other than the thing made. We do not say that they are an act of Allah while the servant is compelled and forced in them, nor do we say they are an act of the servant while Allah is unable over them or does not make the servant a doer of them. Nor do we say that they are created between two creators who independently bring about and effect them.

All these statements are false.

The Qadariyya said: His saying ﴿Allah is the Creator of all things﴾ refers to what no one other than Him is able to do. As for the acts of the servants that the servants are able to do, attributing them to them negates attributing them to Him, and it would necessarily follow that an effect occurs between two agents, which is impossible.

The People of the Sunna said: Attributing them to them as acts and as acquisition (kasb) does not negate attributing them to Him, glorified is He, as creation and will. He, glorified is He, is the One who willed them and created them, and they are the ones who did them and acquired them in reality. For if they were not attributed to His will, power, and creation, their occurrence from them would be impossible, since servants are too weak and feeble to do what Allah has not willed, has not empowered, and has not created.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 39, verse 68:

If it is said: At the blowing into the Trumpet, do the souls remain alive as they are, or do they die and then come to life?

It is said: Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will swoon, except whom Allah wills﴾

So Allah, glorified is He, has excepted some of those in the heavens and on the earth from this swooning.

It has been said: They are the martyrs. This is the view of Abu Hurayra, Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Jubayr.

It has been said: They are Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil and the Angel of Death. This is the view of Muqatil and others.

It has been said: They are those in Paradise, the houris (al-hur al-'in) and others, and among the people, the people of punishment and its guardians. This was stated by Abu Ishaq ibn Shaqla from our companions.

Imam Ahmad has explicitly stated that the houris and the youths (al-wildan) do not die at the blowing into the Trumpet. Allah, glorified is He, has also informed that the people of Paradise ﴿do not taste death therein, except the first death﴾.

This is a text that they do not die except that first death; so if they were to die a second time, there would be two deaths.

As for the words of the people of the Fire: ﴿Our Lord, You have made us die twice and You have given us life twice﴾, their explanation is this verse in al-Baqara, which is His saying: ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah while you were dead and He gave you life; then He will cause you to die and then bring you to life﴾

So they were dead when they were sperm-drops in the loins of their fathers and in the wombs of their mothers; then He gave them life after that, then He caused them to die, then He will bring them to life on the Day of Resurrection. There is in that no causing of their souls to die before the Day of Resurrection, for otherwise there would be three deaths. The swooning of the souls at the blowing into the Trumpet does not necessitate their dying. In the authentic hadith, the people will swoon on the Day of Resurrection, and I will be the first to regain consciousness, and behold, Musa is holding onto a pillar of the Throne, and I do not know whether he regained consciousness before me or was recompensed with the swoon of Mount Sinai.

This is a swoon at the station of the Resurrection, when Allah the Exalted comes to judge, and the earth shines with His light; then all creation swoons, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So leave them until they meet their Day in which they will swoon﴾

If this swoon were a death, it would be another death. Some eminent scholars have noticed this. Abu 'Abd Allah al-Qurtubi said: The apparent meaning of this hadith is that this is a swoon of unconsciousness occurring on the Day of Resurrection, not the swoon of death resulting from the blowing of the Trumpet. He said: My shaykh Ahmad ibn 'Amr said: The apparent meaning of the hadith of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, indicates that this swoon is only after the second blast, the blast of resurrection, while the text of the Qur'an requires that this exception is only after the blast of swooning. Since this is what was said, it is possible that Musa is among those prophets who did not die; but this is false. Al-Qadi 'Iyad said: It is possible that what is meant by this is a swoon of terror after the resurrection, when the heavens and the earth are split; he said: Then the hadiths and reports are reconciled. Abu al-'Abbas al-Qurtubi refuted him, saying: What refutes this is his saying in the authentic hadith that when he comes out of his grave he meets Musa holding onto a pillar of the Throne. He said: This is only at the blast of terror.

Abu 'Abd Allah said: My shaykh Ahmad ibn 'Amr said: What removes this difficulty, Allah willing, is that death is not pure nonexistence; rather it is a transition from one state to another. This is shown by the fact that the martyrs, after their killing and death, are alive with their Lord, receiving provision, rejoicing and glad, and this is the description of the living in this world. If this is the case for the martyrs, the prophets are more deserving and more entitled to it. Moreover, it has been authentically reported from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, that the earth does not consume the bodies of the prophets; and that he, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, met the prophets on the night of the Isra' in Bayt al-Maqdis and in the heavens, especially Musa; and he informed that there is no Muslim who sends greeting upon him except that Allah returns his soul to him until he returns the greeting. Other things besides these that come from its bearers lead to certainty that the death of the prophets is only a return until they are hidden from us, so that we do not perceive them, even though they are existing and alive; and this is like the case of the angels, who are alive and existing though we do not see them. When it is established that they are alive, then when the Trumpet is blown with the blast of swooning, everyone in the heavens and on the earth swoons except whom Allah wills. As for the swooning of non-prophets, it is death; and as for the swooning of the prophets, the more apparent view is that it is a faint. Then when the Trumpet is blown with the blast of resurrection, whoever died is brought to life, and whoever swooned regains consciousness. This is why he, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said in the hadith agreed upon as authentic: "I will be the first to regain consciousness, and our Prophet is the first to come out of his grave before all people except Musa," for there is in it a doubt: whether someone who swooned was resurrected before him, or whether he remained in the state he was in before the blast of swooning, conscious, because he was recompensed with the swoon of Mount Sinai. This is a great virtue of Musa, but one virtue does not necessitate his being absolutely superior to our Prophet, because a particular matter does not establish a general ruling. End of quotation.

Abu 'Abd Allah al-Qurtubi said: If the hadith is taken to refer to the swoon of creation on the Day of Resurrection, there is no difficulty. If it is taken to refer to the swoon of death at the blowing into the Trumpet, then mention of the Day of Resurrection is meant to refer to its beginnings. The meaning is: when the Trumpet is blown with the blast of resurrection, I will be the first to raise my head, and behold, Musa is holding onto one of the pillars of the Throne, and I do not know whether he regained consciousness before me or was recompensed with the swoon of Sinai.

I say: Taking the hadith in this sense is sound, because he, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, was uncertain: did Musa regain consciousness before him, or did he not swoon but was recompensed with the swoon of Sinai?

So the meaning is: I do not know whether he swooned or did not swoon. He said in the hadith: "I will be the first to regain consciousness."

This shows that he, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, swoons along with those who swoon, and that the uncertainty concerned Musa: whether he swooned and regained consciousness before him from his swoon, or did not swoon. If what was meant were the first sense, the swoon of death, then he would have affirmed his death and been uncertain whether Musa died or did not die, and this is false for many reasons. So it is known that it is a swoon of terror, not a swoon of death. In that case the verse does not indicate that all souls die at the first blast; rather it indicates that the death of creatures occurs at the first blast, and whoever has not tasted death before it will taste it then. As for whoever has already tasted death, or whom death was not decreed for, the verse does not indicate that he will die a second death. And Allah knows best.

(If it is said): How do you deal with his saying in the hadith: "The people will swoon on the Day of Resurrection, and I will be the first from whom the earth splits, and I find Musa grasping a pillar of the Throne"?

It is said: There is no doubt that this wording has come in this form, and the difficulty arose from it. But a hadith was inserted into another hadith by a narrator, so that the two wordings were mixed together, and it came out like this. The two hadiths are:

(One): The people will swoon on the Day of Resurrection, and I will be the first to regain consciousness.

(The second), like this: "I will be the first from whom the earth splits on the Day of Resurrection."

In al-Tirmidhi and others, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, he said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "I am the master of the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection, and I say this without boasting; in my hand is the banner of praise, and I say this without boasting; there is no prophet that day, Adam or others, but he is under my banner; and I am the first from whom the earth splits, and I say this without boasting."

Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan sahih hadith.

So this hadith was inserted by the narrator into the other hadith. My shaykh Abu al-Hajjaj al-Hafiz used to say this.

(If it is said): Then how do you deal with his saying: "I do not know whether he regained consciousness before me or was among those whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, excepted," and those whom Allah excepted are excepted only from the swoon of the Trumpet blast, not from the swoon of the Day of Resurrection, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will swoon, except whom Allah wills﴾; and the exception did not occur from the swoon of creation on the Day of Resurrection?

It is said: This, and Allah knows best, is not preserved; it is a mistake by some of the narrators. What is preserved is what the authentic reports agree upon, his saying: "I do not know whether he regained consciousness before me or was recompensed with the swoon of Sinai." Some narrators thought that this swoon was the swoon of the Trumpet blast, and that Musa was included among those excepted from it. This does not fit the context of the hadith at all, for the regaining of consciousness then is the regaining of consciousness of resurrection, so how could he say: "I do not know whether he was resurrected before me or was recompensed with the swoon of Sinai"? Reflect on it.

This is unlike the swoon that creation undergoes on the Day of Resurrection when Allah the Glorified comes to judge between the servants and manifests Himself to them, and they all swoon. As for Musa, peace be upon him, if he did not swoon with them, then he was recompensed with his swoon on the day his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain and made it crumble to dust; so the swoon of that manifestation was made a substitute for the swoon of creation at the manifestation of the Lord on the Day of Resurrection. Reflect on this great meaning, for if there were nothing in this answer but the clarification of this hadith and its matter, it would be fitting to hold onto it with the molars. And to Allah belongs praise and grace, and with Him is success.

The Fire, on the other hand, is the abode of corruption in speech, deeds, food and drink, and the abode of the corrupt. God gathers the corrupt, some of them onto others, piling them up as one piles up things so that they lie one upon another; then He places them in Hell with their own kind, so that there is nothing in it but corruption.

(Section)

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿Those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups, until, when they reach it, its gates will be opened﴾. Its torment and what God has prepared therein overtake them suddenly and catch them unawares. They are like one who stands at a door without knowing what kinds of evil will be opened to him, except that he expects from it some great evil; the door is opened in his face and there befalls him what he had been expecting.

This is like what you find in the world: a man is driven to prison, and its door is closed until he arrives; then the door is opened in his face, and its terror and pain overtake him suddenly, unlike what would be the case had the door been opened for him before his arrival. This is in contrast to the people of Paradise, for since they are driven to the abode of honour, and since it is part of the completeness of honouring a guest who is invited and visiting that the door of the house be opened for him, so that he comes and finds it open, he does not suffer the pain of waiting. Thus, concerning the people of Paradise, He says: ﴿until, when they reach it and its gates have been opened﴾.

The response is omitted to magnify its matter and to glorify its affair, in keeping with their habit of omitting responses for this purpose. This approach relieves you of the claim that the wāw is extra, and of the claim that it is the wāw of eight (wāw al-thamāniyah), because the gates of Paradise are eight. For even if that were sound, it would apply only where the number eight is stated in the wording, one after another, until they reach seven, and then they resume the count from eight with a wāw.

Here there is no mention of the word "eight" in the verse, nor any counting of it, so reflect on this.

Moreover, whether the wāw comes for the eight is a matter of further discussion, which we have mentioned in al-Fath al-Makki, where we explained the places in which it is claimed that the wāw is for eight, and where such a claim is possible and where it is impossible.

If it is said: "Does this not conflict with your view, since the Master of all creation ﷺ comes to the gate of Paradise and finds it closed until he asks for it to be opened?"

We reply: This is part of demonstrating his nobility and excellence over all creatures, that Paradise is closed and is opened for its people only at his hands. Had he come and found it already open, and entered it with its people, the entrants would not have known that its opening was at his hands and that it was he who sought its opening for them. Do you not see that when people seek to enter the gate of a city or fortress and are unable, and it cannot be opened for them until a man comes and opens it for them, at the moment when they most need its opening, there is in that a manifestation of his lordship over them and his excellence and nobility that would not be known had he come with them and they found it open?

We have digressed from the purpose, and how far we have strayed.

Do not find these subtleties burdensome, for you will hardly find them outside this commentary. And God, Exalted, is the Bestower by His grace and generosity.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 39, verse 73:

He follows their entry (into Paradise) with the particle of consequence "fa" (فاء), which indicates that goodness is the cause of entry, meaning: "Because of your goodness it was said to you: enter it, for it is the abode of the good; none enters it but the good."

He said in (Hadi al-Arwah):

He said regarding the people of Paradise: ﴿until, when they reach it and its gates are opened﴾, with the waw (واو).

And he said regarding the description of Hell: ﴿until, when they reach it, its gates are opened﴾, without the waw.

A group said: this is "waw al-thamaniyah" (the waw of eight). It entered the gates of Paradise because they are eight, while the gates of Hell are seven, so the waw did not enter them. This is a weak view with no evidence for it, unknown to the Arabs and to the imams of the Arabic language. It is merely an inference of some later scholars.

Another group said: the waw is superfluous, and the response (jawab) is the verb after it, as in the second verse. This is also weak, for the superfluous waw is not known in their speech, and it is not befitting the most eloquent speech that it contain a superfluous letter with no meaning or benefit.

A third group said: the response is omitted.

And His saying ﴿and its gates were opened﴾ is coordinated with His saying ﴿they reached it﴾, and this is the choice of Abu 'Ubaydah, al-Mubarrad, al-Zajjaj and others.

Al-Mubarrad said: omitting the response is more eloquent according to the people of knowledge.

Abu al-Fath Ibn Jinni said: our companions (the grammarians of our school) reject the superfluity of the waw and do not permit it, and they hold that the response is omitted because it is known.

It remains to be asked: what is the secret in omitting the response in the verse about the people of Paradise, and mentioning it in the verse about the people of Hell?

It is said: this is more eloquent in both places. The angels drive the people of Hell towards it while its gates are closed, until when they reach it, its gates are opened in their faces, so the torment overtakes them suddenly; at the moment they arrive, its gates are opened without delay.

This is the nature of a consequence that follows a condition: that it come immediately after it. Hell is the abode of humiliation and disgrace, so no permission is sought for them to enter it, nor are its keepers asked to enable them to enter.

As for Paradise, it is the abode of God, the abode of His honour, and the place of His elect and friends. When they reach it, they find its gates closed, so they long for its Companion and Owner to open it, and they seek intercession with Him through the resolute messengers (ulu al-azm), all of whom hold back from this until the indication falls upon their seal, their master and their best.

He will say, "I am for it." He will come beneath the Throne and fall down prostrate, and his Lord will leave him prostrate as long as He wills, then He will permit him to raise his head and to ask his need. He will intercede with Him, Glorified is He, to open its gates, and He will grant his intercession, and open it, exalting his station and displaying the rank of His messenger and his honour before Him. For such an abode, which is the abode of the King of kings and Lord of the worlds, is entered only after those great terrors, the first of which begins from the moment the servant comes to his senses in this abode until he reaches it, and what he has ridden of layers upon layer, and what he has endured of hardships upon hardships, until God Most High permits the seal of His prophets and messengers, and the most beloved of His creation to Him, to intercede with Him to open it for them.

This is more eloquent and greater in completing the blessing and achieving joy and delight than what might be imagined otherwise, lest the ignorant man suppose that it is like the inn that anyone may enter. The Paradise of God is lofty and precious, and between people and it lie obstacles, deserts and dangers, which can only be overcome through them. So what of one who follows his soul's desire and wishes vainly of God? Let him turn back from this abode to what is more fitting for him, for he has been created and prepared for something else.

Reflect on what is in the driving of both groups to the two abodes in companies (zumaran): the joy of these people with their brethren and their journeying with them, each company on its own, as partners in a deed, accompanying one another in their company and assembly, rejoicing, strong of heart, just as they were in the world when they gathered upon goodness; thus some of them comfort the others and rejoice in one another. Likewise the people of the other abode: the Fire, they are driven towards it in companies, cursing one another, and some of them harm others. That is more eloquent in disgrace, exposure and shame than being driven one by one.

Do not neglect and reflect on His saying "zumaran" (in companies), and the words of the keepers of Paradise to its people, "Peace be upon you" (salamun alaykum).

They greet them with peace, which includes safety from every evil and disliked thing, meaning: you are safe, so nothing you dislike will reach you after today. Then they said to them, "You are good, so enter it, abiding (therein)" (tibtum fadkhuluha khalidin), meaning: your safety and your entry into Paradise is by your goodness, for God has forbidden it except to the good. So they gave them the good news of safety, goodness, entry and eternity.

As for the people of the Fire, when they reach it in that state of anxiety, grief and sorrow, and its gates are opened for them, they stand before them, and their state is compounded: they are reproached by its keepers and rebuked by them with the words, "Did there not come to you messengers from among you, reciting to you the signs of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your day?" They confess and say, "Yes." Then they are given the good news of entry into the Fire and eternity therein, and that it is an evil abode and an evil return for them.

Reflect on the words of the keepers of Paradise to its people, "Enter it," and the words of the keepers of Hell to its people, "Enter the gates of Hell" (udkhulu abwaba jahannama), and you will find beneath it a subtle secret and a wondrous meaning that is not hidden from the reflective. It is that since Hell is the abode of punishment, and its gates are the most dreadful and most intensely hot of things and the greatest in sorrow, the one who enters it meets with torment even worse than it, and draws near to grief, disgrace, sorrow and distress by entering the gates.

So it was said, "Enter the gates of Hell," as a humiliation for them, abasement and disgrace.

Then it was said to them: your punishment will not be limited to merely entering the dreadful gates, but beyond them is eternity in the Fire.

As for Paradise, it is the abode of honour and the dwelling God prepared for His friends, so they are given the good news from the first moment of entry, of couches, dwellings and eternity therein.

(Section)

Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Baghawi said: Ali narrated to us, Zuhayr informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Asim, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: ﴿And those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in companies﴾, until, when they reach one of its gates, they find beside it a tree from beneath whose trunk two springs flow. They turn to one of them, as if they had been commanded, and drink from it, and God removes from their bellies whatever impurity, harm or ailment there is. Then they turn to the other and wash themselves in it, and the radiance of bliss flows upon them, and their hair never changes thereafter, nor do their heads become dishevelled, as if they had been anointed with oil. Then they reach the keepers of Paradise and say, ﴿Peace be upon you, you are good, so enter it, abiding (therein)﴾.

Then the youths (wildan) meet them, surrounding them as the youths of the people of the world surround the close friend who returns from his absence; they say to him, "Rejoice in what God, Most High, has prepared for you of honour." Then one of those youths sets off to one of his wives of the wide-eyed houris and says, "So-and-so has come, by the name by which he was called in the world."

She says, "Did you see him?"

He says, "I saw him, and he is following my footsteps." So one of them is overcome with joy until she stands at the threshold of her door. When he reaches his dwelling, he looks at the foundation of its building, and there is pearl-dust; above it is a palace of green, red and yellow, of every colour. Then he raises his head and looks at its ceiling, and it is like lightning; had God, Mighty and Majestic, not decreed it, it would have nearly taken away his sight. Then he lowers his head, and there are his wives, cups set out, cushions arranged, and carpets spread. Then they recline and say, ﴿Praise be to God, who guided us to this, and we would not have been guided had God not guided us﴾.

Then a herald calls out: "You will live and never die; you will abide and never depart; you will be healthy and never fall ill forever."

(Section)

God, Glorified is He, has forbidden Paradise to one in whose heart is impurity and corruption, and he enters it only after his goodness and purity. For it is the abode of the good.

Hence it is said to them:

﴿You are good, so enter it, abiding (therein)﴾ [al-Zumar: 73].

That is, enter it because of your goodness. And the good news at death is for these people alone and not others, as God, Most High, said: ﴿Those whom the angels take in death while they are good, saying, "Peace be upon you; enter Paradise for what you used to do"﴾ [al-Nahl: 32].

So Paradise is not entered by one who is corrupt, nor by one who has in him anything of corruption. Whoever purifies himself in this world and meets God pure of his impurities enters it without hindrance. Whoever does not purify himself in this world: if his impurity is intrinsic, like the disbeliever's, he will by no means enter it. If his impurity is acquired and incidental, he enters it after he is purified of that impurity in the Fire, and then he comes out of it, until, when the people of faith have crossed the Sirat, they are detained on a bridge between Paradise and the Fire, where they are refined and cleansed of remnants that remain upon them, which kept them from Paradise yet did not necessitate their entry into the Fire; until, when they are refined and cleansed, permission is granted for them to enter Paradise.

God, Glorified is He, in His wisdom made entry into His presence conditional upon purity, so one who prays does not enter before Him until he is purified. Likewise He made entry into His Paradise conditional upon goodness and purity, so none enters it but the good and pure. Thus there are two purities: purity of the body and purity of the heart. Hence it is prescribed for one who performs ablution to say after his ablution:

"I bear witness that there is no god but God, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and messenger. O God, make me among those who repent, and make me among those who purify themselves."

So the purity of the heart is by repentance, and the purity of the body is by water. When both purities are combined in him, he is fit to enter upon God Most High, to stand before Him and to commune with Him.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 39, verse 75:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And it will be said: "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾

The agent of the verb "it will be said" is omitted, because it is not specified; rather, everyone praises Him for that judgment which He has passed. The heavens and the people of the earth praise Him: the righteous and the wicked, mankind and jinn, even the people of the Fire.

Al-Hasan and others said: "They will have entered the Fire, yet their praise of Him will be in their hearts, and they will find no way to act upon it."

This, and Allah knows best, is the secret for which the agent was omitted in His words:

﴿It will be said: "Enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein"﴾ and in His words: ﴿And it will be said: "Enter the Fire along with those who enter."﴾

As if the whole of creation spoke this and said it to them. And Allah knows best what is correct.

(A subtle point)

The Most High said, following His report of the judgment between His servants, and the destiny of the people of happiness to Paradise and the people of misery to the Fire: ﴿And it will be judged between them with truth, and it will be said: "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾

The agent of "it will be said" is omitted to indicate generality, and that the whole of creation says ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ because of what they witnessed of the wisdom, justice and grace of the Truth.

For this reason He said, concerning the people of the Fire: ﴿It will be said: "Enter the gates of Hell."﴾

As if the whole of creation says that, to the extent that their limbs, their souls, their earth and their heavens say it.
